stdout: usage: bale unlock [-h]
[--reason {abandoned,superseded-by-split,reframed-after-clarification,master-closeout,crash-debris,closed-read-only,no_response,malformed_response,aborted}]
[--force] [--json] [--integration]
[sid]
Close an abandoned session — a `bale pack` that was never applied. Removes the
session's registry entry (its open marker, reconciling the
.bale/current_session pointer) and the matching .bale/sessions/<sid>/
directory; performs no git operations. The sid is optional with exactly one
session open and required when several are open (ADR-0006). Refuses if a
bale/<sid> branch exists — that means `bale apply` ran far enough to create
the branch but didn't reach a terminal state, and the right command for that
state is `bale revert <sid>`. --force overrides the refusal but leaves the
orphan branch in place; delete it with `git branch -D bale/<sid>` if you no
longer want it. --integration instead clears the repo-level integration lock
left stale by an interrupted apply (ADR-0006); it takes no sid and touches no
session.
positional arguments:
sid                   Session ID to unlock. Optional with exactly one
session open; required when several are open. Must
name an open session.
options:
-h, --help            show this help message and exit
--reason {abandoned,superseded-by-split,reframed-after-clarification,master-closeout,crash-debris,closed-read-only,no_response,malformed_response,aborted}
Why this session is closing, stamped into its
telemetry record as closure_reason (BALE.md §8.9).
Omitted, unlock infers: 'closed-read-only' when the
session's recorded scope is empty (a --read-only
pack), 'abandoned' otherwise. An explicit --reason
beats the inference.
--force               Clear the session even if a bale/<sid> branch exists.
The branch is left in place; you'll need to delete it
manually. The override is logged with the FORCE:
prefix.
--json                Emit the end-of-run unlock report as one line of JSON
on stdout — the machine-readable surface for an
orchestrator closing sessions. Stream discipline
matches pack/apply/status --json: '[bale] ' lines and
the human summary block go to stderr, stdout carries
exactly the JSON line; human mode is unchanged.
Emitted on the session-close path and the benign no-op
(outcome 'unlocked' / 'no-op'); the key contract is
owned by format_unlock_json's docstring in
bin/bale_report.py. Session form only: combining with
--integration is refused.
--integration         Clear the repo-level integration lock
(.bale/integration.lock) instead of a session — the
stale-lock recovery for an interrupted apply. Only
safe while no `bale apply` is running. Takes no sid.
